key_value_text.quote: All of the above arguments convinced us that we were in fact looking at neutrino induced events and that 29 of the 34 single track events were muons produced by neutrinos
key_value_text.value: 29 of the 34 single-track events were muons produced by neutrinos; 6 shower candidates were seen against the 2/3 × 29 expected for one neutrino type

name: Observation of High-Energy Neutrino Reactions and the Existence of Two Kinds of Neutrinos
notes: The paper title says "Observation"; the discovery label comes from BNL and the Nobel citation, so the type follows the title (A16).

summary.plain: Using a beam of neutrinos made at Brookhaven's AGS, Danby, Gaillard, Goulianos, Lederman, Mistry, Schwartz and Steinberger saw the neutrinos produce muons but not electrons. That showed the neutrino that goes with the muon is a different particle from the electron's.
summary.technical: High-energy neutrinos from pion decay interacted in a spark chamber to give muons; of 34 single-track events 29 were attributed to neutrino-produced muons, while 6 shower candidates were far fewer than the showers expected for a single neutrino type.

title: Observation of High-Energy Neutrino Reactions and the Existence of Two Kinds of Neutrinos
why_it_matters: The 1988 Nobel Prize in Physics went to Lederman, Schwartz and Steinberger "for the neutrino beam method and the demonstration of the doublet structure of the leptons through the discovery of the muon neutrino"; BNL notes that at the time only the electron-neutrino was known.
